name: Gud Cultures LLC
address: 4951 Upper River Rd, Grants Pass, OR 97526

alpha.desc: The front oblique shows the property's street-facing side with a gravel access area and several mature trees lining the frontage|A green-roofed structure and a larger metal-roofed building are visible near the road|Dense tree canopy partially obscures sightlines to the structures from the street|The gravel yard serves as the primary maneuvering area but is tightly constrained by trees and structures on multiple sides|A long, open agricultural field extends to the rear.

bravo.desc: The right-side oblique reveals the full depth of the parcel — an extremely long, narrow lot running away from the road|The right boundary is open and unfenced along most of its length, with a dirt/gravel perimeter track visible|Three mid-lot storage buildings with light-colored roofs are clustered together|Access to the rear of the property from this side appears to be via an unpaved perimeter track with no formal turnaround visible at the far end.

charlie.desc: The rear oblique shows the far end of the property is open agricultural land with no structures|The perimeter track continues along the right edge but terminates without a formal turnaround|The cluster of storage buildings is visible mid-parcel|The front structures, including the green-roofed building and large metal-roofed structure, are visible in the far background|Vegetation near the front cluster limits rear visibility of those structures from the road.

delta.desc: The left-side oblique confirms the property is an open perimeter on the left boundary — no fencing is visible along the agricultural fields|The large metal-roofed structure at the lower-left (front-right) of the property has a broad footprint with what appear to be storage containers or equipment lined along its side|Dense tree cover around the front structures significantly reduces approach visibility|The gravel area between structures appears limited for large apparatus maneuvering.

considerations: This is a long, narrow commercial agricultural property with a single primary access point from the road at the northern end. The main structures are clustered near the front/road end, surrounded by dense mature trees that restrict visibility and overhead clearance for apparatus. The gravel area between and around the front structures is the only realistic maneuvering zone, and it appears constrained. A perimeter track exists along the right side of the parcel, but it is unpaved and there is no confirmed formal turnaround at the far (south) end of the property. The rear two-thirds of the parcel is open agricultural field with no structures, but access to that area requires traversing the full length of the property. The open perimeter on the left and right flanks means lateral approach to fields is possible but would require cross-country travel over agricultural ground. Large apparatus turnaround near the front cluster is limited by tree placement and structure spacing.
clarifications: 1. Confirm whether the perimeter track on the right side of the parcel can support apparatus weight (surface condition and load rating unknown). 2. Confirm overhead clearance under the tree canopy on the front access approach. 3. Identify whether there is a second road access point at the south/rear end of the property or only the single northern entrance. 4. Clarify the function and occupancy of the three mid-parcel storage buildings and the large metal-roofed front structure. 5. Confirm whether the objects lined along the large front structure are storage containers or other equipment, as they may further restrict apparatus access.
